title: I rebuilt Brood War's rules as a 3D browser RTS with an AI coding agent. Here's what worked and what didn't
author: emilystar_19
selftext:
2149 is a 1v1 RTS against the computer. Three factions (Coalition, Hive, Eidon), ten maps, and the original game's rules: damage types vs unit size, larvae, creep, pylon power, add-ons, lift-off.

How I worked with the agent:

\- I wrote the rules down as data tables first (units, weapons, upgrades, tech requirements) and had the agent build the simulation against them. It runs at a fixed tick with no rendering, so every rule can be tested headless.

\- Tests did most of the heavy lifting: damage formula checks, a test that walks the whole tech tree for every faction, and full AI-vs-AI matches on every map. When the agent "fixed" something, the AI-vs-AI games told me if it broke something else. Larva production got its own regression test after it broke.

\- A map evaluator checks every map and every start pair and renders a top-down image, so I look at pictures instead of numbers.

\- Icons, UI art and unit voice lines are generated. 3D models are low-poly assets plus a few licensed human models; the agent wrote the lighting and ground shaders.

\- The trailer is cut automatically from recorded AI-vs-AI matches: it scores fights by intensity and picks the hottest windows on the music's beat.

What tests didn't catch: things you only see on screen. Air units bobbing up and down with the terrain, larvae hidden inside a neighboring building, Cmd+number control groups switching browser tabs on Mac. Those came from me playing and sending screenshots.

Menus are Korean only for now. Playable link in the comments.
